questions.a: Restaurant feedback management is the ongoing process of collecting, responding to and learning from everything guests tell you. It covers four activities: capturing every guest signal, responding quickly and personally, recovering unhappy guests and acting on recurring patterns. Software helps you do all four across many locations.

questions.q: Why is guest feedback hard to manage at multiple locations?
questions.a: Feedback arrives through reviews, surveys, support tickets, social media and delivery apps, so it's scattered across many places. Writing thoughtful replies to win back unhappy guests takes a lot of time. Without proper analysis, you also can't see how guests really feel or where things went wrong.

questions.q: How do I collect more feedback from restaurant guests?
questions.a: Make it as easy as possible for guests to respond. Short SMS surveys, QR codes on receipts or tables and automated email or SMS requests after a visit all lower the effort. Short surveys tend to pull higher response rates than long-form ones.

questions.q: How can I recover unhappy guests before they leave a bad review?
questions.a: Catch negative feedback early with real-time alerts, then reach out to the guest while the experience is still fresh. Many tools route unhappy guests into a private conversation with your team and send happy guests toward public review sites. A quick, personal response gives you a chance to win the guest back.

questions.q: How much does restaurant feedback management software cost?
questions.a: Prices vary a lot. Some tools publish monthly plans per location, and a few offer free or low-cost entry plans for small restaurants. Many platforms built for multi-location brands use custom quotes, so you'll need to contact sales.

questions.q: Which feedback management software is built for multi-location restaurants?
questions.a: Momos is built for multi-location restaurants and hospitality businesses. It brings reviews, surveys, social messages, email and delivery platform feedback into one Unified Inbox and reads each one for context, sentiment and topics like food quality or wait time. Its AI agent Alfie writes on-brand replies, and its analytics show where incidents happen most.
